+# Homepage analytics
+
+`index.html` loads `analytics.js` with `defer`. It records one `page_view` per
+document load and delegated `click` events, including clicks on non-link content.
+Each event has a millisecond timestamp and the current pathname. Clicks include
+the target tag, a bounded element ID, and the destination pathname for links.
+Text, form values, URL queries, and fragments are not collected.
+
+Provide a same-origin `POST /api/analytics` collector in the deployment (or change
+`ANALYTICS_ENDPOINT` in `analytics.js`). This static repository does not include a
+backend. The collector should accept JSON in this format and return a successful
+status with no response body required:
+
+```json
+{"events":[{"type":"page_view","path":"/","timestamp":1793768400000},{"type":"click","target":{"tag":"a","id":"","href":"/menu"},"path":"/","timestamp":1793768400500}]}
+```
+
+Events reset a one-second inactivity window. Native `fetchLater` requests are
+aborted and replaced with the combined snapshot until delivery activates. A full
+50-event batch is scheduled immediately, bounding the payload well below the
+usual 64 KiB deferred-request limit. Requests omit credentials.
+
+Browsers without `fetchLater`, or whose native scheduling rejects the request,
+use a timer and low-priority keepalive fetch. This fallback also flushes when the
+document becomes hidden or receives `pagehide`, without blocking navigation.
+Delivery is best effort: failed requests are ignored and are not retried.

+are excluded. Fetch requests omit credentials.

+requests are dropped without retries, and events beyond the queue limit are
+dropped. Tracking does not delay or cancel navigation.

+# The Daily Grind
+
+Static homepage with a responsive delivery-notes workspace. The checked-in `assets/app.js` bundle runs directly from the existing static host. Rebuild after changes to `src/`:
+
+```sh
+pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
+pnpm run build
+```
+
+No application server or database is required for this demo.
+
+## Delivery notes
+
+- Standard: ephemeral X25519 key agreement.
+- Post-quantum: ML-KEM-768 encapsulation using `@noble/post-quantum`.
+- Hybrid (default): the library's X-Wing combination of ML-KEM-768 and X25519.
+- All options derive a per-note AES-256-GCM key using HKDF-SHA-256 with a fresh random 32-byte salt and domain-specific context. Every encryption uses a random 12-byte nonce and a 128-bit authentication tag.
+- The version, note ID, mode, algorithm, recipient fingerprint, timestamp, encapsulation, salt, and nonce are authenticated as additional data. Saving performs an authenticated decrypt round trip before retaining the envelope.
+- Reveal decrypts a note and can show the complete encrypted envelope. Delete removes it. User text is rendered as text, never HTML.
+
+This is explicitly a **local demonstration**, not an integrated delivery service. Encrypted envelopes and demo recipient private keys stay in memory. Nothing is sent to a courier; no notes or keys are written to browser storage. Closing or reloading the page clears the session. JavaScript string memory cannot be reliably zeroed; byte-array secrets are cleared after use where feasible. HTTPS (or localhost) and Web Crypto are required, with no plaintext fallback.
+
+A real integration must obtain authenticated recipient public keys from the delivery service, keep recipient private keys with the intended recipient, and send only the encrypted envelope to a backend. The local reveal functionality demonstrates decryption and is not a recipient access boundary.
+
+The homepage uses an Unsplash coffee photograph and Google Fonts. Crypto dependencies are bundled locally rather than loaded from a runtime CDN.

+# Script performance diagnostics
+
+The page loads `script-performance.js` with `defer`. It uses the Long Animation
+Frames API to attribute JavaScript execution in frames that take over 50 ms.
+Buffered observation includes available frames from before the observer started.
+
+In a supporting browser, use the site normally and inspect the developer console.
+Scripts accumulating at least 100 ms in slow frames are logged as a table, at most
+once every five seconds when new frames arrive. No data is sent or persisted.
+
+To inspect the current ranking manually:
+
+```js
+console.table(window.scriptPerformance.report());
+// Include every observed source, even below the 100 ms reporting threshold:
+console.table(window.scriptPerformance.report({ minDuration: 0 }));
+// Check support and collection status:
+window.scriptPerformance.status;
+// Stop collecting while retaining the report:
+window.scriptPerformance.stop();
+```
+
+Results are sorted by `totalDuration`, the cumulative execution time attributed
+to a source in slow frames. `invocations` counts attributed script entries;
+`longestDuration` is the longest observed invocation, and
+`forcedStyleAndLayoutDuration` highlights synchronous style/layout work. All
+durations are in milliseconds. Reports return copies and drain queued entries.

+These measurements identify optimization candidates, not proof that a script
+alone caused a slow frame. They are not total script execution time, network
+download time, or an INP measurement. Cross-origin and other unavailable
+attributions may be omitted by the browser; missing source URLs appear as
+`(unattributed script)`. Inline scripts can be attributed to the document URL.

+report does not prove there are no performance issues. This static page currently
+has no application scripts besides the diagnostics, so an empty report is normal.
+Storage is capped at 200 distinct sources per page visit; additional sources are
+skipped and counted in `status.droppedAttributions`.

+# Homepage INP monitoring
+
+The homepage loads `scripts/inp.js` as a deferred ES module. It uses Google's
+self-hosted `web-vitals` attribution build, version **6.2.3**, with its Apache 2.0
+license in `scripts/vendor/web-vitals.LICENSE`. No install or build is required.

+
+## Connect field collection
+
+Set the existing meta tag in `index.html` to a real, same-origin analytics POST
+endpoint, for example:
+
+```html
+<meta name="inp-report-endpoint" content="/analytics/web-vitals">
+```
+
+That route must be provided by your hosting platform or analytics service; this
+static repository has no backend. An empty value (the default) sends no network
+requests. Monitoring still runs and emits `daily-grind:inp` on `window`, with the
+plain report in `event.detail`, for integration with an existing analytics agent.
+Configure one collection path to avoid duplicate ingestion. The collector should
+accept JSON POSTs and return a success response such as 204. If a consent system
+is required by your deployment, gate the module loading through that system.
+
+Reports use `sendBeacon`, with `fetch({ keepalive: true })` as fallback when beacon
+is absent, throws or refuses the payload. Delivery is best effort, with no retry
+queue. Script/frame details and strings are bounded to keep reports small.
+No external runtime CDN requests or persistent client identifiers are introduced.
+
+## Report contents and analysis
+
+Every report includes the INP value in milliseconds, rating, delta, metric ID,
+navigation type, report timestamp, and page pathname. Interaction details include
+a fixed `data-inp-target` label, pointer/keyboard type, time, next-paint time and
+load state. Labels cover every existing homepage link, including nested targets.
+Unknown controls use `unlabeled`; the monitor does not collect text or input values.
+Page queries/fragments and script URL credentials/queries/fragments are excluded.
+
+`phases` breaks INP into input delay, event processing duration and presentation
+delay. For available Long Animation Frame (LoAF) data, reports also include:
+
+- `longestScript`: URL, function, source character position, invoker, duration,
+  forced style/layout duration, the dominant INP subpart, and intersecting duration.
+- `scripts`: the ten scripts with the largest overlap with this INP interval,
+  with separate overlap durations for each phase. Scripts outside the interval
+  are excluded. Overlaps describe timing correlation, not proof of causation.
+- `rendering`: the library's script, style/layout, paint and unattributed totals
+  for the INP interval. Paint duration represents off-main-thread presentation
+  delay; the API cannot separately identify GPU, raster and compositor work.
+- `frames`: up to five related frames with render/style-layout start times,
+  duration and blocking duration. These raw frame durations can extend outside
+  INP; do not sum them with INP phases or script durations. Forced layout is
+  already included in the rendering style/layout total.
+- `omittedScripts` / `omittedFrames`: detail counts omitted from the payload.
+
+The library reports on visibility hidden (including navigation) and handles
+back/forward cache restores. It measures the page's INP candidate, not every slow
+click. Keep the latest report by `id` and `reportedAt` before calculating visit
+percentiles; repeated reports for a visit are updates, not separate samples.
+Back/forward cache restores get a new metric ID. Aggregate the visit-level p75,
+and group slow visits (`value > 200`) by target, phase and script URL/function.
+Values over 500 ms are poor; 200–500 ms need improvement.
+
+Browsers lacking Event Timing produce no report. Without LoAF support, INP and
+its three phases still work, but script/rendering attribution may be unavailable.
+`longAnimationFramesSupported` distinguishes unsupported browsers from supported
+browsers with no captured long frame. Missing rendering totals remain absent,
+not zero. LoAF captures frames over 50 ms and script entries over 5 ms; cross-origin
+scripts may have restricted details. Visits without interactions do not produce
+INP samples and must not be counted as zero.

+attribution, URL sanitization, missing attribution, payload bounds, transport

+# Daily Grind performance audit
+
+Audited November 4, 2026. Scope: all application files in this repository.
+Verification uses source inspection, downloaded asset sizes, and an offline
+performance budget check. No browser, development server, preview server, or
+server entrypoint was run. This static project has no build script.
+
+## Findings and changes
+
+| Area | Finding | Change / result |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| LCP discovery | The likely LCP photo was only referenced in CSS, with no priority hint. | A standard HTML image exposes the resource to the preload scanner, with `fetchpriority="high"`. It is not lazy loaded. No redundant preload is needed. |
+| Image transfer | Every viewport requested a remote 1350px image. | Three same-origin WebP candidates let the browser choose a size using viewport width and pixel density. The largest candidate retains the original resolution. |
+| Connections | The image required another origin's DNS, TLS, and availability. | Checked-in assets remove the Unsplash connection from visitors' loading path. |
+| CLS | The background already had a reserved hero height. | Preserve that reservation, add a minimum height for short viewports, and declare image dimensions. The absolutely positioned photo cannot displace text as it loads. |
+| Narrow screens | The navigation could exceed the viewport; the grid had a fixed 250px minimum. | Navigation wraps in normal flow, and cards can shrink below 250px when needed. All navigation remains available without a script-driven menu. |
+| INP | No JavaScript, event handlers, loops, timers, hydration, or layout-reading code exists. | Keep native links and zero runtime JavaScript. There is no identified application long task to split or debounce. |
+| Rendering | Tiny DOM, small inline stylesheet, system fonts, no third-party scripts. | Retain this inexpensive rendering path. Avoid introducing bundles, font downloads, workers, service workers, or containment overhead. |
+| Interaction motion | Color transitions are the only animations. | Honor reduced-motion preferences without introducing runtime work. |
+
+The hero retains the same stock photograph, centered cover crop, dark overlay,
+and text. It has an empty alt attribute because it is decorative.
+`sizes="max(100vw, 90vh, 30rem)"` accounts for the photo's 3:2 aspect ratio
+covering a full-width, 60vh hero with a 20rem minimum height. A portrait viewport
+can need a source wider than the viewport to avoid an undersized cover crop.
+WebP is supported by current major browsers; priority hints degrade to normal
+browser heuristics without requiring JavaScript.
+
+## Measured transfer sizes
+
+The baseline image was fetched from the exact original URL with a client that
+received JPEG. Unsplash's `auto=format` may return another format for browser
+clients, so these percentages are a comparison against that fetched JPEG,
+not a claim about every visitor's prior transfer size.
+
+| Asset | Bytes | Reduction from fetched original |
+| --- | ---: | ---: |
+| Original 1350px JPEG | 157,969 | — |
+| New 640px WebP | 37,728 | 76.1% |
+| New 960px WebP | 72,922 | 53.8% |
+| New 1350px WebP | 123,438 | 21.9% |
+
+The browser selects one candidate, rather than downloading all three. Actual
+selection depends on viewport dimensions, device pixel ratio, and browser
+heuristics; mobile does not always select the smallest candidate.
+
+The HTML remains below 6 KB uncompressed and 2 KB in a local gzip estimate.
+There are no external CSS files, font requests, or client scripts. This is still
+a two-resource page (document plus photo). Compression estimates are not proof
+of deployed compression.
+
+## Reproducible verification
+
+Run `npm run audit:performance` (requires Python 3; no package installation).
+The offline check verifies:
+
+- HTML stays within 10 KiB and the page ships no JavaScript or external stylesheet.
+- The hero is responsive, discoverable in HTML, dimensioned, and high priority.
+- A high-priority image is never lazy loaded.
+- Every referenced candidate exists locally and has a WebP signature.
+- The 640px candidate stays within 40 KiB and all others within 128,000 bytes.
+- CSS does not introduce external resource origins.
+
+`git diff --check` also passes. These checks catch loading regressions; they do
+not measure rendering, image appearance, field responsiveness, or Core Web Vitals.
+
+## Deployment and remaining verification
+
+Hosting configuration is not present, so response headers, compression, TTFB,
+CDN behavior, and real-user performance could not be verified or changed here.
+
+- Enable Brotli or gzip for HTML at the host. WebP is already compressed.
+- Revalidate HTML with `Cache-Control: no-cache`. Cache images with an appropriate
+  lifetime; use content-hashed/versioned filenames before applying a year-long
+  `immutable` policy. These current filenames must be revalidated when changed.
+- Serve the document and assets over HTTPS with HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 where supported.
+- Ensure deployment includes `assets/*.webp` and serves them as `image/webp`.
+- Confirm the linked menu, account, order, and other routes exist in the deployed
+  application. This repository contains only the landing page, so destination
+  response times and interactions are outside the available source.
+- After deployment, assess real-user data at the 75th percentile, separately for
+  mobile and desktop. Targets: LCP ≤2.5s, INP ≤200ms, CLS ≤0.1. No before/after
+  timings or Lighthouse score are asserted by this audit.
+
+Platform guidance used: the `performance` and `optimize-image-priority` guides
+from the project's modern-web-guidance skill. The `break-up-long-tasks` guide
+was reviewed but required no changes because the page has no JavaScript.

+# Daily Grind performance audit
+
+## Scope and evidence
+
+Audited the entire supplied site: `index.html`, package scripts, resource loading,
+layout, and navigation. This repository contains one static page, no JavaScript,
+no dependencies, and no build script. No browser, development/preview server,
+server entrypoint, or Lighthouse session was used. This is a source and asset
+audit; it does not establish measured Core Web Vitals or a Lighthouse score.
+
+## Findings and changes
+
+| Area | Finding | Implemented optimization |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) | The full-width hero used a CSS background, discovered after CSS processing, with a single remote 1350px JPEG for every device. | Use a parser-discoverable image with `fetchpriority="high"`, eager loading, and three responsive WebP candidates hosted locally. This removes the image's cross-origin connection and third-party availability dependency. |
+| Transfer size | The original Unsplash response was 157,969 bytes. | Reuse the same stock photo, compressed to 32,258–100,138 bytes. |
+| Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) | The hero already reserved height, and system fonts avoided font swapping. Mobile viewport changes could resize its `vh` height. | Preserve reserved space, add intrinsic image dimensions, and use stable `svh` units with a `vh` fallback. The image remains absolutely positioned so loading cannot push content down. |
+| Interaction to Next Paint (INP) | No scripts, event handlers, hydration, long tasks, or interaction libraries exist in the supplied page. | Preserve native link interactions and zero JavaScript. No script-driven interaction delay could be identified from source. |
+| Mobile interactions | Navigation could overflow because neither flex row wrapped. Small links were harder to tap. | Wrap navigation, provide 44px-tall navigation links, and keep the card grid within narrow viewports. |
+| Rendering and accessibility | Small inline CSS and system fonts already kept the critical path short. | Retain that architecture; add visible keyboard focus and honor reduced-motion preferences. |
+
+An image preload was intentionally omitted: the image is already in the initial
+HTML after a small inline stylesheet. A second resource declaration adds
+maintenance overhead without an established benefit for this page.
+
+## Asset results
+
+| Asset | Bytes | Reduction vs original |
+| --- | ---: | ---: |
+| Original remote JPEG, 1350 × 900 | 157,969 | — |
+| Local WebP, 640 × 427 | 32,258 | 79.6% |
+| Local WebP, 960 × 640 | 56,230 | 64.4% |
+| Local WebP, 1350 × 900 | 100,138 | 36.6% |
+
+The HTML is 5,576 bytes before transport compression. A cold load transfers one
+HTML document and one selected image: approximately 37.8–105.7 kB uncompressed,
+excluding headers. Browsers select the image using viewport width and pixel
+density; small screens with high pixel density can select the larger candidates.
+The maximum image resolution remains equal to the original site's resolution.
+
+Photo source: the existing site's [Unsplash stock image](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1495474472287-4d71bcdd2085).
+The local variants were fetched from that image service using WebP output and
+quality 60. No new image generation service or runtime image transformation is
+required.
+
+## Validation performed
+
+- Parsed the HTML and confirmed all image source references resolve locally.
+- Inspected WebP binary headers and confirmed that actual dimensions match every
+  `srcset` width descriptor.
+- Confirmed intrinsic dimensions, eager loading, and high fetch priority for the
+  hero; no duplicate CSS background request remains.
+- Checked budgets of less than 10 kB for HTML and 110 kB for each image.
+- Confirmed zero JavaScript, external render resources, and blocking external
+  stylesheets.
+- Ran `git diff --check` successfully. There is no build script to run.
+
+Responsive behavior, visual quality, keyboard focus appearance, and real loading
+and interaction timings have not been verified in a browser, as requested.
+
+## Deployment follow-up
+
+These items depend on the production host and cannot be established from this
+repository:
+
+1. Enable Brotli or gzip for HTML. Serve the WebP files as `image/webp`; they are
+   already compressed and do not need additional transport compression.
+2. Use HTML revalidation (`Cache-Control: no-cache`) and a suitable image cache
+   lifetime. Use content-versioned filenames before enabling year-long immutable
+   image caching. The current descriptive filenames must be invalidated or
+   changed when replacing their contents.
+3. Serve static assets through the site's CDN and verify cache hits, TLS, and
+   response times. TTFB and production caching were not measured here.
+4. Confirm the existing navigation destinations are served by production. The
+   repository contains no `/menu`, `/locations`, account, checkout, or other
+   linked route implementations; their response and interaction performance
+   cannot be audited from this page.
+5. After deployment, use existing field data (CrUX, Search Console, or your real
+   user monitoring) to evaluate the 75th percentile separately for mobile and
+   desktop: LCP ≤ 2.5 seconds, INP ≤ 200 milliseconds, and CLS ≤ 0.1. These are
+   acceptance targets, not claimed results. Use field evidence to decide whether
+   any further optimization or instrumentation is necessary.
